newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Army commander General Chettha Thanajaro has told troops to exercise restraint in settling border conflicts with Burma. The order follows a confrontation after a Burmese unit was deployed on a disputed islet in the Moei River to protect to a dredging crew. At some points, the troops were a few metres from each other. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The New Aspiration Party (NAP) declines to announce support for the new constitution, saying the draft still contains several "unacceptable" points which first need to be changed. The party director says the NAP cannot follow the example of the Democrats, who has announced unconditional support for the charter draft. (THE NATION)

- The Civil Service Commission has come up with incentives to encourage early retirement as part of the government's efforts towards bureaucratic reform, commission officials say. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who chaired the Civil Service Commission meeting yesterday, agreed with these proposed incentives to lure public servants into early retirement. (THE NATION)

- Government agencies vehemently denied anything went on behind the scenes at the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) yesterday, where a computer malfunction, suspended share trading for four hours. Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan strongly denounced those who accused the government of orchestrating the suspension of trading three minutes after the market opened. (THE NATION)

- The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) is planning to launch a government promotion campaign "Amazing Thailand" during 1998-1999 to boost the local tourism industry. A government official reveals that the TAT board chaired by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has considered problems and obstacles concerning tourism. It has thus implemented several methods to support the industry. (BUSINESS DAY)
